title: Side-Lying Hip Abduction
summary: A side-lying leg raise for the glute medius. It needs no equipment.

muscles.why: Library rating 0.9 for abductors (main mover): each working set adds 0.9 of a set to the weekly abductors total.
Library rating 0.25 for obliques (minor): each working set adds 0.25 of a set to the weekly obliques total.

setup.text: Lie on your side with your legs stacked and straight.
Rotate your top leg's toes slightly down.
Raise your top leg to about 30–45°.

form_cues.cue: Lift the top leg toward the ceiling
Keep your hips stacked. Don't roll back.

mistakes.text: Rolling the hips back so the leg swings forward.

lower_risk.text: Warm-up: the app adds no ramp-up sets; make the first working set a touch lighter if you like.
The app suggests a heavier load only when the jump is 10% or less; otherwise it adds a rep first.
Default target: 10-15 reps, stopping about 2 reps short of failure (RIR 2). Stop the set when form breaks down.
Use the same controlled range on every rep; lower under control rather than dropping or bouncing.
Pick a variation and range you can train pain-free.

alternatives.why: Swap sheet: Better isolation, More stable, Steadier cable tension.
Swap sheet: Better isolation, More stable, Both sides together.
